stories.headline: New England No.1? James Trafford tipped by Leeds boss
stories.summary: Daniel Farke praised James Trafford's potential following a solid display in Leeds' 0-0 draw against Sunderland.
stories.body:
Daniel Farke praised James Trafford's potential following a solid display in Leeds' 0-0 draw against Sunderland.

The 24-year-old goalkeeper twice denied Black Cats striker Brian Brobbey in the first half and was called into action again after the break to stop Nilson Angulo.

Trafford joined Leeds from Manchester City over the summer for a reported fee of £40 million ($53m) plus bonuses and Farke was impressed with his display as the Yorkshire side secured a clean sheet.

"I wouldn't say there was an unbelievable, world class save, but several good saves and he has shown also today why we were so desperate to sign him," Farke said.

"Yes, his natural belief and skills, his aura and confidence also inspires the players in front of him but to be honest, I was expecting a performance like this from him, this is why we spent some money on him.

"I expect also a goalkeeper for Leeds on this level in a difficult away game to be the here and there. I don't expect anything less than the performance that he showed today.

"Of course, he's for me the most promising young goalkeeper in the UK and he has all potential, more or less, to be also one day England's No. 1.

"He shows this capability for us day in, week in, week out, but he has to keep going and show this with consistency. Again, I expect performances like this because he has potential to do this and nevertheless, we are all happy to have him."

stories.headline: Bafana boss Pitso Mosimane's latest South Africa squad shows favouritism fears were unfounded
stories.summary: Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.
stories.body:
When Pitso Mosimane returned as Bafana Bafana head coach, sceptics feared that his proximity to South African club football would lead to an erosion of the meritocratic culture Hugo Broos had built, but the 62-year-old's second preliminary squad suggests it has only been enhanced.

Mosimane began his tenure with Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying wins over Guinea and Eritrea and a friendly victory over Egypt. Next up is the AFCON qualifying double-header against Kenya on Nov. 13 & 17.

Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.

Chicago Fire's Mbekezeli Mbokazi has returned from injury, while Aden McCarthy, Botiumelo Radiopane, Nqaba Xulu, Luke le Roux, Thalente Mbatha, Nkosikhona Radebe, Devin Titus and Thakasani Mbanjwa have also received call-ups.

For every one of these call-ups, a layman can deduce a clear possible motive. McCarthy is the most obvious among them -- he has consistently featured at centre-back for Sabah in the UEFA Champions League and performed well at the highest level.

Radiopane and Xulu are in hot scoring form domestically for Orlando Pirates and Richards Bay respectively. Titus has earned his place with a strong start to life at MAS Fes in Morocco. Mbatha is back from injury and le Roux on the books of a new club at Cercle Brugge after struggling for game time at Portsmouth.

Radebe adds a right-back option from an in-form AmaZulu side with Mamelodi Sundowns' Khuliso Mudau still on the mend from injury. Mbanjwa is rewarded for a strong start to the season in goal for Golden Arrows.

Yanela Mbuthuma and Shandre Campbell -- both of whom have experienced dips in form and fortune at club level since the last international break -- are notable absentees.

In cutting two players he had given opportunities to after they had been mostly overlooked by Broos, Mosimane suggested he is willing to operate without fear or favour.

When 'Jingles' was on the verge of being appointed, Broos was quoted as telling Het Nieuwsblad: "You know, South Africa still don't have a coach. The candidate is Pitso Mosimane, a successful South African coach.

"But they know that if he comes in, they'll go five years back in time. Club owners and agents calling coaches to influence the squad selection. I threw all of them out. If one called, I would say bluntly: 'I don't talk with agents'."

The concern over agents and owners trying their luck in influencing the Bafana head coach may have been well-founded. Broos was not the first to complain of this within the national team setup.

However, questioning if Mosimane himself was open to influence without proof he was willing to make publicly available was ill-advised. It is impossible to accurately speculate on what conversations have or have not gone on between Mosimane and club owners and agents in the two months since then, but what is clear is that his team selection has been thoroughly meritocratic.

The momentum he has garnered is reminiscent of what Broos achieved in the first six months of his tenure.

At the time, the Belgian's irreverent team selection and approach to squad culture put everybody on their toes and led to an uptick in results. After they had failed to qualify for AFCON 2021 immediately before Broos was appointed, the Belgian fell narrowly short of steering Bafana into qualification playoffs for the 2022 World Cup.

In subsequent years, he kicked on and led Bafana to third place at AFCON 2023 (held belatedly in Ivory Coast in early 2024) and the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

When discussing the most successful Bafana Bafana coaches of all-time, Broos should be placed alongside Clive Barker in the top two. However, even the brightest tacticians eventually settle on patterns in their squad selection, and towards the end of his tenure, the Belgian became more predictable in certain aspects.

There was a fairly settled back five of Ronwen Williams, Aubrey Modiba, Mbokazi, Ime Okon and Mudau, and until he switched up his attacking plan to revive the FIFA World Cup campaign, Broos was likely to start Lyle Foster upfront with Evidence Makgopa the main alternative.

In midfield, Teboho Mokoena was a near certain starter and Sphephelo Sithole the clear preferred option alongside him, although Broos occasionally tinkered with his formation and left room for the likes of Bathusi Aubaas and the late Jayden Adams in the holding role. Nkosinathi Sibisi was considered another option, occasionally stepping out from the back into midfield.

Mosimane's arrival has reopened competition for places in these positions. Brooklyn Poggenpoel is retained in the squad after impressing in midfield over the last international break.

After Mbuthuma's minutes upfront, Radiopane and Xulu have been given a chance to earn theirs. Foster has made a second successive preliminary squad, although he failed to make the final squad last time out while in the process of leaving Burnley on loan to Houston Dynamo and settling in.

Fawaaz Basadien, Olwethu Makhanya, and McCarthy are in consideration in the backline. Mudau is, however, still the likely first-choice at right-back for the time being when he returns to full fitness. Still, Mosimane has done well to identify alternatives.

Mosimane declined to get drawn into a war of words with Broos over anything not directly related to matters on the pitch and instead praised his predecessor's impressive record as Bafana head coach.

In his first stint, Mosimane may not have succeeded in the hotseat. However, early results and his approach to team selection suggest he has justified the decision of the South African Football Association (SAFA) to give him a second chance and trust him to navigate the role without fear or favour to anyone.

stories.headline: George Russell: Finishing second in F1 title race 'doesn't mean anything'
stories.summary: George Russell says finishing second in the championship would not mean anything as boss Toto Wolff hit back at suggestions that the British driver may never get another shot at the title.
stories.body:
George Russell says finishing second in the championship would not mean anything as boss Toto Wolff hit back at suggestions that the British driver may never get another shot at the title.

The 28-year-old trudged home eighth at the United States Grand Prix on Sunday, the bare minimum he needed to keep the title race mathematically alive as leader Kimi Antonelli roared to a dominant victory.

Antonelli now holds a whopping 123-point lead over his team-mate, with Lewis Hamilton still just about in it a point further back. Russell also now has Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc within 10 points of him.

While the Italian is likely to be celebrating the championship in Mexico City next weekend, Russell is not driven by the fight to finish second.

"As long as we win the constructors' championship, that's the main thing," a dejected Russell said.

"Obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest but P2, P3, P5 is not champion, so it doesn't mean anything."

Antonelli was in a league of his own in Austin, romping home a huge 13.0 seconds ahead of Leclerc.

But Russell, hampered by an early five-second penalty, had no answer in the same machinery, unable to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri to progress from eighth.

- F1 readies Antonelli's title champagne in Austin: 'The race of a champion who isn't champion yet'

- F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?

"Six good laps, 50 bad laps," Russell added. "The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that's the least of my worries after such a bad weekend.

"He obviously was exceptionally competitive and there are signs that the window [of performance] is very small. I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace today, but I need to believe in my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off."

Russell entered the season as heavy title favourite in the grid's dominant car but his young teammate has turned the tables and is set to storm to the title.

Former Red Bull motorsport advisor Helmut Marko told Sky Deutschland this week that he doubted Russell would ever get another shot at the championship, having been usurped as Mercedes' number one.

Team principal Wolff hit back at that assertion, saying: "I think he's [Marko] wrong on George. George has all the ability. I think the car doesn't suit him.

"I think that at the beginning of the season it's difficult to cope with a situation where you're feeling like 'this is my year to come', and then you have this wunderkind on the other side that starts to really chip away.

"And I believe that in a new season, George, if we provide him a quick car, has absolutely what it needs to win a championship."

Wolff also believes it is down to the team to understand Russell's deficit to Antonelli, taking blame away from his driver.

"George, for all of us in the team, is a champion and has won in every category. I think he merits to be put in the group of the very best ones," Wolff added.

"This year we see this variability in results. When we land the car in the way that suits him, he's absolutely fine.

"But when it drops out of the operational window, he struggles. He struggles more than maybe Kimi. And that is on us.

"We just have to work it out. Because George is not half a second slower, three tenths slower than Kimi. That's just absolutely not the case.

"So what is it that he doesn't like? What is it that we need to do in terms of modifying the car, setting it up in a different way for him to go fast? Because it's all there -- intelligence, ability, determination."

stories.headline: Who I would -- and would not -- want to be this AFL offseason
stories.summary: The AFL offseason is in full swing but it won't stop us from analysing the landscape. Here's who Jake Michaels would (and wouldn't!) want to be heading into 2027.
stories.body:
From Brisbane's stunning three-peat to Fremantle's Grand Final capitulation, high-profile free agent signings to ongoing legal battles, so much has happened in the AFL world over the past month. So, who would you want to be (and not want to be) this off-season.

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Those I WOULD NOT want to be this AFL offseason
Ross Lyon
No coach will enter season 2027 under more scrutiny and pressure than Ross Lyon. St Kilda was widely tipped to rise up the ladder this season just gone after being the most active club during the previous trade and free agency period. Instead, the Saints severely underwhelmed, winning just 10 games and finishing a disappointing 11th on the ladder, 10 premiership points outside of the wildcard finals. The club is desperate to retain the services of superstar midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera, who is out of contract at season's end and could easily be tempted with a blockbuster move back to South Australia. As a result, St Kilda's powerbrokers likely won't tolerate another sluggish start, which means Lyon has absolutely zero margin for error in 2027.

Fremantle fans
Alright, alright, I'm sorry to bring it up again. And please feel free to skip ahead if you don't want to re-live it once more. But the reality is every single Dockers fan will be replaying those harrowing final four-and-a-bit minutes of the Grand Final in their mind all offseason, wondering how on earth their team coughed up what appeared to be an insurmountable late lead. The heartbreaking loss to Brisbane is as devastating as it gets for a footy club and you could almost understand if any Fremantle fan never wanted to watch the sport again. Seriously, I'm not sure how you ever get over that loss. It all just means the next five months are going to feel like an eternity.

Andrew McGrath
It was an incredibly disappointing season from new Essendon skipper Andrew McGrath, who averaged a career-low in disposals, kicked just two goals, and failed to poll a single Brownlow Medal vote. To be a captain of a club that won just two games for the entire year and still be unable to crack the top 10 of the best and fairest count is pretty embarrassing, really. With former skipper Zach Merrett now no longer at the club, McGrath, who has now been in the league for a decade and tallied 200 games, is Essendon's main man. It's time he starts to play like it or else he risks further damage to his reputation.

Chris Fagan's replacement
Whoever is entrusted with the task of succeeding Chris Fagan at the Lions will be feeling the pressure and the eyes of the footy world on them from day one. It's a bit like following Jerry Seinfeld on stage. How can you possibly back up that act!? Fagan completely revitalised Brisbane, leading the club out of the doldrums and to its second three-peat this century. And while Fagan's tenure is up and dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale has departed for Collingwood, nobody feels as if the Lions are over the hump. In fact, quite the contrary. The age profile of this list should have them contending for years to come. That can be both a blessing or a curse for any new coach.

The Pullman Five

Okay, this one might be a tad on the nose, but who would want to be one of Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice, or James Jordan this offseason? The incident at the Pullman Hotel in Melbourne on the eve of finals remains a legal matter, meaning there are still so many unknowns when it comes to the footballing careers of these five. Can Heeney and Warner ever ingratiate themselves to the Swans' faithful once more? Will Bice and Jordan be shuffled out of the best team? And then there's Blakey. North Melbourne gave up the farm for his signature and much will be expected of him at his new club. I'm just not sure he's the difference maker they think he is.

An (existing and competing) expansion club
At what point do we stop referring to Gold Coast and GWS as expansion clubs? Probably now. But I'm lumping them together in here for different reasons. The Suns were a total shambles this year, falling from flag favourite after three rounds to finishing in the bottom six and winning just two games after the mid-season byes. Spearhead Ben King has now departed the club and rumour has it Matt Rowell wants to follow suit. Damien Hardwick is under the pump and must show something in year four at the helm. Meanwhile, the Giants just held a fire sale, clearing out Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs. It's a bold move, and while it could pay dividends down the track, you figure there simply has to be some short term pain.

Those I WOULD want to be this AFL offseason
Zach Merrett
This time last year Merrett would have been top of my other list, but the veteran midfielder's wish of a fresh start at a new club has now been granted, and that must feel like an enormous weight has been lifted from his shoulders. Merrett joins the Hawks, a club which could easily have won the premiership this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's late heroics during preliminary final weekend. It means that for the first time in Merrett's career he will enter a season truly believing his side can go all the way. That's got to be a great feeling for an elite player who has toiled away for so long and enjoyed little success.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera
As we've established, his coach might be under immense pressure, but Wanganeen-Milera certainly shouldn't be feeling the pinch. In fact, he goes into next season with all options and possibilities on the table. If the Saints turn out to make good on their promise from last year and actually show they can compete with those at the pointy end, then he may well elect to sign on and remain at the club. But if 2027 turns out to be more of the same, he will have his choice of 17 new destinations to call home, including the two clubs from his home state of South Australia. Make no mistake, Wanganeen-Milera will be both the most discussed and in-demand player in the sport next season.

Andrew Mackie and Geelong's entire recruitment staff
When the siren sounded on the trade and free agency period, Geelong list boss Andrew Mackie should have been pumping his fists and popping bottles of champagne in celebration. The Cats have been arguably the biggest winners of the offseason to date, improving across every line with additions of former Giants captain Toby Greene, reliable ruck Rowan Marshall, and still criminally underrated key defender Jordan Ridley. It's a hefty haul and a great salvage after the club discovered at the eleventh hour it would be missing out on the services of Zak Butters. Mackie and his team have done their job, now it's over to Chris Scott and the playing group.

Fremantle fans
Alright, so there are the obvious reasons why you wouldn't want to be a Fremantle fan this offseason, but there are also plenty of reasons why you absolutely would. The Dockers came within an inch of winning their first premiership last month and proved to the footy world, and their supporters, the club has a list to not only go all the way in 2027 but remain one of the premier sides in the league for the next half decade. Just about everyone on this Fremantle squad is yet to hit their prime and has serious scope to improve next year. That should be both a worrying thought for the other 17 clubs and a great comfort to those who cheer for the men in purple.

Jason Horne-Francis
The departure of superstar midfielder Zak Butters during free agency means the keys to Port Adelaide now firmly belong to Horne-Francis. Some might argue he's shared those keys with Butters in recent years, but there's simply no denying who will be top dog at Port heading into next season. Horne-Francis is still just 23 years of age but he has shown he possesses all of the attributes to succeed as his club's main man. I expect him to relish the extra responsibility, too, and take his game to even greater heights. Jason, train hard and we'll see you in 2027!

Jaymie Graham
It must feel pretty special knowing a club made the decision to part ways with a four-time premiership-winning coach in favour of you, despite the fact you've never coached a senior AFL game. Graham arrives at Arden Street with an impressive resume as an assistant and has been tasked with ending North Melbourne's decade-long finals drought. Some will make the case he faces similar pressure to whoever takes over from Fagan at the Lions, but I see his role, at least in the immediate future, as one which carries far less of a burden. Given North's recent struggles, he will be offered (a little) time to get things right. His team is also in the sweet spot of being enough to win with now but not good enough to carry crazy expectation.

stories.headline: Time, place unclear for Game 6 of Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals
stories.summary: With the Valkyries forcing a Game 6 in the WNBA Finals, the Dream are working to resolve a scheduling issue that leaves the venue and time of the game up in the air.
stories.body:
After the Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday in Atlanta's State Farm Arena, tying the best-of-seven series at 2-2, one question was answered and another far more important question was raised.

There will be a Game 6 in Atlanta. But nobody knows where or even when the game will be played despite a furious round of negotiations spilling into Sunday between the WNBA, NBA, Valkyries, Dream and Atlanta Hawks, sources told ESPN.

The Dream -- whose home venue of Gateway Center Arena has a capacity of approximately 3,500 -- have played all five home playoff games at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, home to and operated by the Hawks. Coordination between the leagues, teams and multiple media partners resulted in Games 3 and 4 of the Finals getting moved to State Farm Arena. Game 3 was shifted up a day, from Thursday to Wednesday, while the Hawks agreed to hold a doubleheader with the Dream and moved tip time of Saturday evening's home opener back 30 minutes.

But with the Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm the night of Game 6, along with other scheduling complications, the situation is more complex than what the leagues dealt with earlier in the series and could have millions of dollars of impact on both leagues.

"We continue to explore all options," a WNBA spokesperson told ESPN.

Said a Dream spokesperson: "We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena. If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena."

Sources believe it's a real possibility that Game 6 will be held Thursday as scheduled at Gateway Center Arena in College Park.

"There are problems with all the solutions," one source close to the situation said.

Sources told ESPN that the NBA has been working with the Hawks and Cavaliers to determine if Thursday's game could be switched to an alternate date -- or even to Cleveland. While some stakeholders feel the onus should be on the NBA to move its regular-season game so the WNBA Finals can be prioritized, there has been pushback from others that the domino effects of moving that game are too complicated.

Thursday's Cavaliers-Hawks game is already a back-to-back for both teams: The Hawks host the Miami Heat at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, when the Cavaliers play a home game before traveling to Atlanta.

Moving Thursday's game to Cleveland is a radical idea that has been discussed, sources said, but it would create a home-road back-to-back for the Hawks in addition to the logistical nightmare of scheduling a new home game in Cleveland with just a few days' notice.

Following Thursday's game, Cleveland is supposed to play Saturday in Milwaukee, which could also be hosting Game 7 of the World Series. Fridays are NBA Cup exclusive games, while Hawks-Cavaliers is a non-Cup game.

State Farm Arena has open dates on Tuesday -- the day after Golden State hosts Game 5 -- and Friday. One proposal would move Game 6 of the WNBA Finals to Friday and Game 7, if necessary, from Saturday, Oct. 31, at Chase Center to Tuesday, Nov. 3.

The WNBA would support that proposal, but only if both teams agree to it, sources said.

The Valkyries have raised concerns about moving two WNBA Finals games and the three off days that proposal would create in between Games 5 and 6 as well as between Games 6 and 7, sources said.

"We're proud to be part of such a compelling Finals and love seeing the growth of the game," a Valkyries spokesperson said in a statement. "We fully support what's best for the league and will stand behind whatever it decides."

Playing Game 7 on Nov. 3 would conflict with a recent NBA policy of not holding games on Election Day, although sources said that does not currently appear to be a strong concern.

Availability at Chase Center is also not abundant. The Golden State Warriors -- whose ownership group also owns the Valkyries -- have home games scheduled against the LA Clippers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2.

While they don't share an ownership group with the Dream, the Hawks have expressed a desire to help facilitate the WNBA Finals in their arena, as they did for Games 3 and 4, sources said. The Dream will be a full-time tenant at State Farm Arena beginning in 2027, the team announced earlier this month, which should make holding playoff dates in the future more seamless.

There has been discussion about moving Thursday's game to a matinee, like Game 4 was, sources said. The Hawks have been open to facilitating another doubleheader at State Farm Arena, but other sources said the WNBA believes the idea of a weekday matinee for a Finals game would not be as desirable compared to a weekend matinee.

Other Atlanta-area alternate arenas -- such as Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion or Gas South Arena in Duluth -- aren't viewed as ideal since they would feel like road games for both teams.

Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta sold out quickly once they were moved to State Farm Arena. Fans wanting to purchase tickets for Game 6 have been told to wait for a resolution to the scheduling conflicts, sources said.

While it is not uncommon for WNBA playoff games to be moved to alternate sites because of arena commitments to NBA games or other events, sources on all sides of this situation expressed frustration that these issues hadn't been resolved before Saturday.

"This should've been solved weeks ago, and definitely at the same time Games 3 and 4 were solved," one source said.

Said another: "The fact we are making these decisions so we can play a WNBA game at a larger arena is the best news of all. ... It just has to be scheduled better in advance. Moving games is much harder now than it would have been a week ago."

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Saturday's hero: Forget Sal Frelick's offensive numbers. The guy is a folk hero in Milwaukee. This was true before Saturday, but it's reached Bunyanesque proportions after Frelick smacked a game-tying homer in the sixth inning of Game 2. That evened the score at four and completed the Brewers' comeback from a four-run deficit. Frelick's fourth-inning single also contributed to the Brewers' third run. There were a lot of big momentum swings in Game 2, but nothing got the ballpark rocking like Frelick's blast.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cochrane set for Ipswich Jets; Samrani to test open market
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Who could replace Carrick after Man United's worst start since 1986?
stories.summary: Manchester United have struggled this season, but which managers could step in to replace Michael Carrick if the club sacks him?
stories.body:
Editor's note: This story first ran on Oct. 21 as Manchester United's dismal 2026-27 season got even worse with a 1-1 draw to Leeds United. Since then, United lost 4-1 to Como in the Champions League, followed by a 3-0 defeat to AFC Bournemouth in the Premier League.

Manchester United have made their worst start to a league season since 1986. They exited the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle last month and are closer to the Premier League relegation zone than the top four following the 1-1 draw at Leeds United on Oct. 19, so the pressure is mounting on manager Michael Carrick.

That trip to Elland Road extended United's winless run in all competitions to six games, though Carrick said that the result against Daniel Farke's side marked a "fresh start" for his team. But Wednesday's UEFA Champions League trip to Serie A's Como provided no respite, as United hit a new low with the 4-1 loss.

United have dismissed a manager in each of the past two seasons -- Erik ten Hag was fired in October 2024, followed by Ruben Amorim in January 2026.

So with results continuing to disappoint and Carrick, who guided United to Champions League qualification as interim manager last season, struggling to prove he is the man for the job in the long term, who are the most likely candidates to replace the 45-year-old at Old Trafford if he fails to inspire a change of fortune?

Here are the managers who could be on United's radar -- and the prospects of them being the next one to take on one of the sport's biggest, and toughest, jobs.

Eddie Howe (unattached)
Positives
The 48-year-old is taking a break from the game after stepping down as Newcastle United manager in August following almost five years in charge. During his time at St James' Park, Howe saved the club from relegation before guiding the team to Champions League qualification on two occasions and ending a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025.

Howe is a proven Premier League manager with a track record at Newcastle and Bournemouth. He is a team builder, tactically astute and his ability to transform the fortunes of players like Joelinton and Dan Burn at Newcastle would appeal to United, whose squad is stacked with players who are failing to live up to their potential. Another key element with Howe is his immediate availability.

Negatives
Howe will deliver stability and consistency wherever he manages, but does he possess the X factor for a club of United's magnitude? That is perhaps a harsh question to ask of a coach whose credentials are without question, but United need a coach to lift the whole club and its fan base. Howe's "Steady Eddie" persona might be exactly what they need, but also what they really don't need right now.

That strange dilemma is probably why United are in the mess they are in. They need the stability and calmness -- and direction -- that Howe would bring, but they also need a personality to become the focal point and leader of a club that has lost direction. Howe wins on the basics, but United need more than that.

Suitability rating
3/5: Howe would be a sensible appointment, but that isn't enough for Manchester United.

Antonio Conte (unattached)

Positives
Since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, United have hired seven managers and only one -- José Mourinho -- arrived at Old Trafford having previously won, or even competed for, the Premier League title. Conte's 2016-17 triumph with Chelsea would put him in the Mourinho category as a proven winner. The 57-year-old has also won Serie A titles with Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and domestic cups in Italy and England, so if United want to hire somebody with a glittering CV, Conte can certainly point to an array of success.

He is also a coach who has made an instant impact at many of his previous clubs, winning the title in his first season at Chelsea and Napoli and initially starting well at Tottenham Hotspur. So the short, sharp shock of a Conte appointment could jolt the United squad into a rapid improvement. And like Howe, Conte is available after leaving Napoli in the summer.

Negatives
The problem with Conte is that there are plenty of negatives. Many would argue that they outweigh the positives. The former Italy coach is confrontational with his players and also those in the boardroom, while the majority of his previous jobs have ended in acrimony.

If Carrick goes, United might want somebody to get tough with the underperforming squad. Conte would do that, but his ultra-demanding approach could have a negative effect on a group of players that has rarely shown toughness, so a bad situation could become worse. Since leaving Juventus for the Italy job in 2014, Conte has had four club jobs and never lasted more than two years in any of them, so if United want a long-term solution then he isn't their man.

Suitability rating
2/5: It would be lively at United under Conte, but he's just too abrasive to make it work.

Kieran McKenna (unattached)

Positives
The former Ipswich Town manager would be the inexpensive and inoffensive option for United. At 40, McKenna is a young coach with a big future having earned three promotions with Ipswich after leaving his role as first-team coach at Old Trafford to take charge of then-League One side in December 2021.

McKenna's success at Portman Road saw him short-listed for the Chelsea job in May 2024 before missing out to Enzo Maresca, but after standing down at Ipswich this summer, his availability and familiarity with United would appeal to the Old Trafford hierarchy. If United want a coach with a level-headed personality to work within their existing structure, McKenna would be a good fit.

Negatives
In many ways, if United replaced Carrick with McKenna it would be a like-for-like change. If he returned to Old Trafford, working once again with players including Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot and Marcus Rashford, would it be enough of a change or simply a different face delivering the same message?

McKenna lacks Carrick's credentials as a top-class player, but his managerial success to date would balance that out. McKenna's one season in the Premier League ended in relegation, so that would not sit well with a club of United's stature. McKenna might be a future United manager, but right now he needs to take another step before really being an option for one of the world's biggest clubs.

Suitability rating
2/5: Too inexperienced and too similar to Carrick.

Fabian Hürzeler (Brighton & Hove Albion)

Positives
The 33-year-old has built a sensational young team at Brighton that are now threatening to challenge for the Premier League title and maybe even emulate Leicester City's shock success in 2016. Hürzeler, who became the youngest-ever Premier League coach when he arrived from St Pauli as a 31-year-old in 2024, has benefited from Brighton's renowned recruitment department. But his coaching and tactical acumen has developed the team and turned the Seagulls into a high-energy, aggressive and confident side.

Last month's 3-0 win against champions Arsenal proved their ability to compete with the best. And if United are looking for ability and personality, Hürzeler's active sideline presence is a key part of his makeup and Brighton's performances. His outspoken criticism of Mikel Arteta's tactics at Arsenal last season highlighted his readiness to take on the leading coaches.

Negatives
Having signed a three-year contract extension at Brighton in May, United would be faced with a hefty compensation bill for Hürzeler and that could put him out of the running due to the financial restrictions imposed by Old Trafford minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. At such a young age, Hürzeler also has question marks over his experience and readiness for a job as big as United, whose gamble on the 39-year-old Amorim two years ago backfired spectacularly.

Hürzeler's high-energy philosophy would be unlikely to work with a United squad that is the second oldest in the Premier League and his spiky personality might also clash with director of football Jason Wilcox, not to mention the team's senior players.

Suitability rating
4/5: Maybe the right coach at the wrong time, but if United want to be bold and exciting then Hürzeler should be their guy.

Julian Nagelsmann (unattached)

Positives
The 39-year-old is out of work, available and with a point to prove after failing to succeed in his last two jobs with Germany and Bayern Munich. Nagelsmann earned his status as one of Europe's rising coaching stars with success at Hoffenheim and RB Leipzig before moving to Bayern at the age of just 33 in 2021.

He is regarded as a big thinker tactically and a coach with laser-like focus on detail, so he could bring much needed cohesion and clarity to the United team.

Negatives
Nagelsmann is available because his last two jobs didn't work out and they were big jobs of a similar stature to the one at United, so one of the question marks over him is whether he has the attributes to coach at the highest level or if his qualities are better suited to clubs with smaller budgets and more limited ambitions.

His time at Bayern ended badly amid reports of clashes with senior players and it was a similar story this summer following Germany's round-of-32 exit from the FIFA World Cup. Nagelsmann is young enough to bounce back, learn from his last two experiences and succeed again, but United is probably not the environment for a coach to rehabilitate himself.

Suitability rating
1/5: Too much of a risk on both sides for Nagelsmann and United to work out.

Thomas Tuchel (England)

Positives
Tuchel is a big-name coach with the character and self-confidence to take on the United job without any sense of fear or trepidation. He has won domestic titles in France and Germany with Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich and also guided Chelsea to Champions League success in 2021, so Tuchel ticks every box for United.

If United want to hire a proven winner with a personality to match his track record, then Tuchel -- who was interviewed for the job in 2024 -- is the perfect fit.

Negatives
Plenty. First of all, Tuchel is the England manager and he extended his contract earlier this year to tie him to the job until the end of Euro 2028, so the 53-year-old is as close to unattainable as possible. But even if Tuchel and the English Football Association parted company in the months ahead, Tuchel's reputation for clashing with players and owners would make him a high-risk appointment for United.

When Tuchel spoke to United at the end of the 2023-24 season, an agreement between both parties was close until talks broke down, so the prospect of everyone returning to the table and expecting a different outcome would appear unlikely.

Suitability rating
4/5: If available, Tuchel would be ideal for United, despite the negatives. But while he remains England manager, there is no chance of him heading to Old Trafford.

The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

stories.headline: LAFC clinches playoffs with derby draw, Galaxy cling to last spot
stories.summary: Leo Walta scored the tying goal in the 62nd minute as LAFC clinched a playoff spot by rallying from two goals down in the second half for a 2-2 draw with the LA Galaxy on Sunday night.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Leo Walta scored the tying goal in the 62nd minute as LAFC clinched a playoff spot by rallying from two goals down in the second half for a 2-2 draw with the LA Galaxy on Sunday night.

Joseph Paintsil scored his first two goals since August as the Galaxy hung on impressively for a point, but endangered their own playoff hopes by blowing the lead in another thrilling El Tráfico derby.

The final seconds of injury time were breathtaking: Galaxy goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski and defender Justin Haak both made spectacular stops on LAFC chances before Denis Bouanga scored on a redirection of Tyler Boyd's bicycle kick -- only for the play to be ruled offside.

Bouanga scored the first goal for LAFC, which is headed to the MLS playoffs for the eighth time in its nine seasons of existence. LAFC is currently sixth in the Western Conference standings, while the Galaxy sit ninth.

The rivalry series between the two teams remains even at 10 wins and 10 losses apiece with eight draws.

LAFC has produced one win and three draws from four matches since interim head coach Xavi Tamarit took over for the fired Marc Dos Santos on Oct. 1.

Son Heung-Min thought he had scored on a rebound of Bouanga's shot midway through the first half, but the play was ruled offside and confirmed by a lengthy video review. Moments later, Robert Taylor intercepted a pass and set up Paintsil to hammer home his first goal in a competitive match since Aug. 19.

Painstil doubled the Galaxy's lead in the 51st minute when Hugo Lloris spilled a rebound directly to him. LAFC fans threw drinks at the celebrating Galaxy players after both of their goals.

But just two minutes later, LAFC's Armindo Sieb ripped a shot from off a counterattack and Bouanga chipped home the rebound for his 18th goal in 30 MLS matches this season.

LAFC remained on the attack and tied it when Emiro Garces' defensive misplay allowed Walta to score his second goal in the Finland international's four matches with the club.

The Galaxy played without star German midfielder Marco Reus, a late scratch due to illness. Striker Hirving "Chucky" Lozano is also out with a hamstring injury that occurred during international duty with Mexico.

stories.headline: F1 readies Antonelli's title champagne in Austin: 'The race of a champion who isn't champion yet'
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli isn't F1 world champion just yet, but after winning in Austin on Sunday, it's only a matter of time for Mercedes' winderkind.
stories.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- The closer Kimi Antonelli gets to making Formula 1 history, the less he seems to care about the enormity of what he's doing.

Antonelli's ninth win of 2026 at the U.S. Grand Prix left him a whisker away from the F1 championship; to claim the crown, he needed Lewis Hamilton to finish fifth or lower (he finished fourth) and George Russell to finish ninth or lower (he finished eighth). He now needs just two points in Mexico -- a ninth-place finish will suffice -- to finally become the youngest driver to clinch the title and the first Italian to do it since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

All the talk coming into the race had focused on Antonelli's chance of getting it done. You wouldn't have known it -- the 20-year-old was the personification of cool from his arrival in America this week. Toto Wolff explained it best, recalling a chat with his driver before the race.

"I was just asked was he nervous before the race," the Mercedes boss said to Sky Sports immediately after Antonelli's win. "He sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, 'I'm going to enjoy this ride now. It's weird I'm not thinking about the championship at all, isn't that funny?' So he's on a discovery mission in terms of what's happening with him emotionally. He delivered from the beginning to the end. It was exceptional."

It certainly was, and it was also an event that nicely summed up the year of each protagonist involved. Out in front, Antonelli was wonderful, taking a great pole on Saturday and then scampering clear on Sunday, the unstoppable prodigy who just doesn't know where the limit is. Behind him, Mercedes' three closest rivals -- Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, each with two wins to their names this year -- fought for scraps in a back-and-forth battle for best of the rest, one eventually decided by tire wear and strategy calls.

And then there was poor old Russell, who endured another miserable weekend in Antonelli's shadow. The Briton -- once upon a time, in a galaxy far, far away, the 2026 preseason title favorite -- was outqualified by Antonelli by nearly half a second on Saturday and then crossed the line nearly 55 seconds behind on Sunday. The race was Russell's season summed up in little more than 90 minutes. Already on the back foot, his chances of clawing back into the contest were undone by a five-second penalty that pushed him even further down the order at a crucial phase of the race.

"The penalty was a bit ridiculous," a deflated Russell said later. "But yeah, the least of my worries after such a bad weekend."

Much like the bad luck that has been an undeniable story in Russell's season so far, the penalty did not dramatically change the outcome, but it was a kick in the gut to a driver already down on the canvas and effectively out for the count.

Rubbing salt into the wounds for Russell would have been that his miserable weekend wasn't quite miserable enough. By finishing eighth, and not ninth, he is still mathematically in a title fight he knows he's lost for another week.

Kimi's crowning moment
The history books will not remember Austin as the official coronation, but it might as well have been.

A different tire choice to Max Verstappen promised a thrilling start; Verstappen and Red Bull had opted for the grippier soft tire, but Antonelli's getaway on the medium was flawless and he scampered clear. He only briefly gave up the lead as the different strategies intertwined at mid distance, but the outcome of the race was never in doubt. It was as comprehensive a performance as you will see.

To Wolff, who has already steered two Mercedes drivers to world championships, it was Antonelli's best of the bunch in 2026.

"On Kimi's side, obviously that is the main headline: for me, the best race that he's delivered so far," Wolff said on Sunday evening. "Getting off the start with the inferior tire and then controlling it at all times. The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional."

In terms of the stopwatch, it wasn't quite his most dominant of his nine wins: he beat Oscar Piastri by 13.7 seconds at the Japanese Grand Prix in April and crossed 13.078s clear of Charles Leclerc on Sunday. But in terms of feel, there's no contest: it was as complete a drive you will find. As he spoke to the media, Wolff was reminded of another candidate for the champion-in-waiting's best win: his thrilling Italian Grand Prix victory in September, where he stormed from 19th on the grid. That felt special for a number of reasons, not least the outpouring of emotions after the race.

"Both of them were pretty good," Wolff said in reply. "But the headline that this is the best, we can keep."

Take your pick: Monza and Austin will both stand out as special moments in Antonelli's special season, and there's a case to be made for either one.

For what it's worth, even with the emotional high of becoming the first Italian winner in Italy since 1966, he seemed to suggest Austin felt more special because of the circumstances involved.

"I mean, Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," Antonelli said when asked to compare the two. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back, but it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake and we were so quick. But definitely, Monza was a super special one, and one that I will remember forever. But, you know, this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good."

Staying grounded in this remarkable year has been the number one priority for Antonelli, and it shows. As he told ESPN on the eve of Austin's race, he still visits the pub and goes to the bowling alley with his friends in San Marino; he's also picked up the religious habit of washing his road car by hand every day before he travels to his next race. It's all helped Antonelli bounce back from a nightmare rookie season last year.

Wolff, who signed F1's next world champion when he was just 11 years old and has overseen the significant financial investment Mercedes has made in him since, has been blown away by the development.

"There are many people that said last year after nine races without points, he shouldn't be in a Mercedes. People in other teams that said he shouldn't even be in Formula 1," the Mercedes CEO said. "And all of that now is extremely satisfying to see what he's able to deliver. How he's working with the team, with [race engineer Peter Bonnington] and yielding the results. But it wasn't an easy road. So I'm happy that, like you say, 99.9%. He still needs to finish the race in Mexico."

Antonelli made a similar point on Sunday night. His achievements and performances on track have been staggering, but his approach to life and Formula 1 in the eye of the storm has been just as impressive. He alluded to how much work has gone in behind the scenes to make his imminent championship a reality.

"I'm very lucky because I have a very good group of people around me," he said when asked whether he had surprised himself by delivering so well on a week that had so singularly focused on his chance of becoming champion. "In the team, I have my father, who always comes, then my performance coach. I just have a great group of people around me that help me to be more relaxed and not worry about these kinds of things. They help me to block out the noise, and that's also what's been allowing me to enjoy the weekend and perform.

"I think, obviously, there's been a lot of talk. I'm not going to lie, on Thursday there was a lot of talk about the championship and stuff, and I just tried not to worry about that at all and just tried to deliver the best result I could. Today was a very important result for me and for the team."

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.
